The specification describes a project related to Spring Cloud Stream (based on the modules mentioned: json-tuple processor, script processor, splitter processor, gauge sink, aggregate-counter sink, field-value-counter sink, hdfs-dataset sink, mail sink). These are all modules from Spring Cloud Stream Apps.

The user stories (U1-U8) are all about adding acceptance test coverage for various processor and sink modules so they can be validated in CI builds.

This is essentially a QA/testing task - adding acceptance tests to 8 different modules.

Let me break this down:

1. Each module needs acceptance test coverage
2. This involves understanding each module's functionality
3. Writing test cases
4. Setting up test infrastructure if needed
5. Integrating with CI build

Let me create a WBS:

1. Setup/Test infrastructure (common)
   - Review existing test patterns/conventions
   - Setup test framework configuration
   
2. Per module activities:
   - Understand module functionality
   - Write acceptance test cases
   - Implement test code
   - Verify tests pass in CI

3. Integration
   - Configure all tests in CI pipeline
   - Final verification

Let me estimate:

Common setup: 2-3 days
Per module: 
- Simple processor/sink (json-tuple, script, scripts, splitter, gauge, aggregate-counter, field-value-counter): 1-2 days each
- Complex sink (hdfs-dataset, mail): 2-3 days each (these need external services like HDFS and mail server)

json-tuple processor - relatively simple JSON transformation - 1.5 days
script processor - 1.5 days (simpler)

mail sink - 2 days (needs mail server setup)

Plus common infrastructure: 2-3 days

1. Use existing Spring Cloud Stream Apps test framework/patterns
2. Implement tests as integration tests using the test binder
3. Use TestContainers for external dependencies (HDFS, mail server)
4. Tests should be runnable in CI with Maven/Gradle
5. Each module gets its own test class(es) following existing conventions
6. Use JUnit 5 and Spring Boot Test
7. Add module configuration to parent CI build

1. The project already has a test framework structure in place
2. A test binder is available for testing
3. The modules are well-documented with clear expected behaviors
4. CI build is already configured (just need to add modules)
5. The developer is familiar with Spring Cloud Stream

technical_and_design_decisions: Use the existing acceptance test framework conventions already established in the Spring Cloud Stream Apps project (JUnit 5, Spring Boot Test, TestBinder).
Use Testcontainers to provide external dependencies (e.g., HDFS, SMTP/MailHog) for sinks that require external systems, ensuring tests are self-contained and CI-runnable.
Implement one acceptance test class per module, following the established patterns of the project to keep the code consistent with the rest of the suite.
Tests will be wired into the existing Maven module structure and the parent CI build invocation, so they run automatically on every build.
Tests will cover the primary happy-path scenarios of each module plus the most representative error/edge cases (e.g., missing required properties, invalid inputs, empty payloads).
Effort assumes the developer is familiar with Spring Cloud Stream and the existing acceptance test infrastructure of the repository.
assumptions: A standard 8-hour workday is used for the estimates.
An acceptance test framework (TestBinder, base test classes, Maven plugins for IT/surefire) is already in place; only module-specific additions are required.
Module source code and configuration metadata are already available; the work is limited to writing and integrating acceptance tests, not implementing or fixing module functionality.
hdfs-dataset and mail sinks require external services; they will be containerized for the tests (Testcontainers), assuming Docker is available in the CI build environment.
Default scope of 'acceptance test coverage' means at least one end-to-end test per module covering the typical use case, plus a couple of representative negative cases.
The 'script' and 'scripts' processor modules are treated together in U2 but will be implemented as two separate test classes (one per module), with shared helpers to avoid duplication.
No new CI infrastructure (Jenkins/GitHub Actions pipeline definition changes) is required beyond updating the module list that the parent build aggregates.
No documentation updates beyond standard test javadocs are in scope.

activities.activity_name: Review existing acceptance test framework and conventions
activities.activity_description: Inspect existing acceptance test base classes, TestBinder usage, Maven configuration (failsafe, profiles) and any module test conventions so the new tests follow established patterns.

activities.activity_name: Create shared test helpers and infrastructure (containers, properties)
activities.activity_description: Add reusable test utilities, e.g. Testcontainers definitions for HDFS and SMTP/MailHog, and common property builders, to be reused by the sink tests that need external systems.

activities.activity_name: Add acceptance tests for json-tuple processor module
activities.activity_description: Implement an acceptance test class covering the json-tuple processor: send sample JSON payloads, verify transformed tuple output, and cover a representative negative case.

activities.activity_name: Add acceptance tests for script processor module
activities.activity_description: Implement an acceptance test class covering the script processor: supply a script expression, send input payloads, verify resulting message payloads.

activities.activity_name: Add acceptance tests for scripts processor module
activities.activity_description: Implement an acceptance test class covering the scripts processor (multi-script pipeline): send input, verify that the chained scripts transform the message as expected.

activities.activity_name: Add acceptance tests for splitter processor module
activities.activity_description: Implement an acceptance test class covering the splitter processor: send a composite payload, verify it is split into the expected number of messages with the expected content.

activities.activity_name: Add acceptance tests for gauge sink module
activities.activity_description: Implement an acceptance test class covering the gauge sink: send a metric-bearing message, verify the metric is registered/updated on the metrics endpoint.

activities.activity_name: Add acceptance tests for aggregate-counter sink module
activities.activity_description: Implement an acceptance test class covering the aggregate-counter sink: send a series of messages, verify the aggregated count is exposed via the metrics endpoint.

activities.activity_name: Add acceptance tests for field-value-counter sink module
activities.activity_description: Implement an acceptance test class covering the field-value-counter sink: send messages with field values, verify the per-value counts are exposed via the metrics endpoint.

activities.activity_name: Add acceptance tests for hdfs-dataset sink module
activities.activity_description: Implement an acceptance test class using a Testcontainers-based HDFS instance: write messages, verify dataset files/partitions are produced in HDFS with expected content and roll-over behavior.

activities.activity_name: Add acceptance tests for mail sink module
activities.activity_description: Implement an acceptance test class using a Testcontainers-based SMTP catcher (e.g., MailHog/GreenMail): trigger mail messages, verify the SMTP server received the expected emails with correct subject, body and recipient.

activities.activity_name: Wire new test modules into the parent CI build
activities.activity_description: Update the parent POM / Maven aggregator and CI pipeline configuration so all new acceptance test modules are executed on every CI build, including container-enabled profile activation.
Run the full CI build locally and in the CI environment, fix any flakiness or configuration issues, and ensure all eight new acceptance test modules are part of every CI build.
